picks.intervention_label: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on Sanai phase 0/2, MGMT-stratified (NCT07485049)
picks.rationale: This is the trial the patient's preference file was written for. The free-text says "surface all possible options" with efficacy lean 0.7 and prefers_trials true, and the single best-mechanism-matched trial currently recruiting for newly diagnosed MTAP-null IDH-wildtype GBM is the Sanai phase 0/2 at Ivy/Phoenix. MGMT stratification is baked into the design (Arm A unmethylated = BGB-58067 + RT; Arm B methylated = BGB-58067 + RT + TMZ), which means the trial slot also resolves the unmethylated-vs-methylated branching decision the team has to make anyway. Anvumetostat's MTAPESTRY-101 readout (Rodon AnnOnc 2024, Cancer Discovery 2025) gives the class an ORR ~11% in a heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null cohort with grade >=3 TRAE 13.8% and discontinuation 2.5% (cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record so far), but BGB-58067 is the asset built for CNS exposure after TNG908 was discontinued in November 2024 specifically because CSF sampling confirmed inadequate brain exposure. No toxicity veto in the preference file. The honest weak spot is geographic: this is a single US site in Phoenix and the patient will need to travel.
primary_concerns: Eligibility gated on MTAP IHC on the resection block (target_validation essential row) and willingness to undergo a phase 0 re-resection biopsy for SDMA / H-score readout; the subtotal-resection block may have enough tumor cellularity but the intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation could have compromised that, so pathology has to confirm before counting on the Phase 0 slot.
Geographic move to Phoenix is the practical hurdle. No modality constraint in the preferences file blocks travel, but it is a real logistic.

Trial-first preference fully satisfied; efficacy lean honored by mechanism-matched targeted therapy with a brain-penetrant agent; no toxicity vetoes triggered; intratumoral-hemorrhage history is not a contraindication on this trial.

picks.intervention_label: Stupp regimen: RT 60 Gy/30 fx + concurrent TMZ 75 mg/m^2/day + 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ 150-200 mg/m^2 days 1-5 q28d (standard of care anchor)
picks.rationale: The preferences file says surface SoC and the Stupp backbone is the OS-anchored standard for newly diagnosed IDH-WT GBM: HR 0.63 for OS at the EORTC 26981 primary readout (mOS 14.6 vs 12.1 mo) and 5-year OS 9.8% vs 1.9% on long-term follow-up. The honest read is that the OS benefit concentrates in MGMT-methylated tumors per Hegi 2005 (methylated mOS 21.7 vs 15.3; unmethylated mOS 12.7 vs 11.8 with no statistically significant gain), which is why MGMT methylation is the high-priority diagnostic gap to resolve before the adjuvant commitment is finalized. At age 66 ECOG 1 the patient is inside the EORTC 26981 enrolled population. This pick is non-negotiable as the backbone; the question is whether to layer trial enrollment (pick 1) on top, swap to CeTeG (pick 4) if MGMT comes back methylated, or substitute Perry hypofractionated RT if fitness changes.
primary_concerns: MGMT methylation status is UNKNOWN and is the dominant effect modifier; methylation-specific PCR or pyrosequencing has to be ordered if not already in flight (target_validation essential row).
Grade 3-4 hematologic AE 7% during concurrent and 14% during adjuvant phase per Stupp 2005; PJP prophylaxis during concurrent phase because of lymphopenia. All on-label.
Preference fit: SoC framing explicitly requested in the free-text; efficacy lean honored; no veto on TMZ; modality (RT + oral TMZ) silent in preferences.

picks.intervention_label: Tumor-treating fields (Optune, 200 kHz) added to adjuvant TMZ per EF-14 schedule
picks.rationale: EF-14 phase 3 hit OS HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001), mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, and 5-year OS 13% vs 5% added on top of adjuvant TMZ alone. Approved device, no trial enrollment needed, no overlapping systemic toxicity (52% any-grade scalp dermatitis under the arrays, 2% grade 3 is the headline AE). The efficacy gain is real and the preference file's 0.7 efficacy lean with no modality veto makes it the easy add. The practical commitment is the >=18 hr/day wear-time, which the team should counsel on up front. The OS benefit holds across MGMT subgroups, so this layers cleanly on either branch of the MGMT decision.
primary_concerns: Adherence to >=18 hr/day wear-time is the binding factor for the EF-14 effect size; sub-18-hour wear cuts the benefit roughly in half per the per-protocol analyses.

Trial-prefer preference would also support TRIDENT (NCT04471844, TTFields-during-RT) but enrollment closed February 2026 and the readout is pending — the on-label EF-14 schedule is what the patient can act on now.
Compatible with picks 1, 2, 4 and does not conflict with any active trial enrollment I can identify in the dossier.

picks.intervention_label: CeTeG / NOA-09 lomustine + TMZ + RT (conditional on MGMT methylated)
picks.rationale: If MGMT comes back methylated, CeTeG is the largest published OS signal in newly diagnosed GBM: mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, p=0.049 one-sided per-protocol). That is a 16.7-month OS gain over standard Stupp in the methylated stratum. The efficacy lean at 0.7 plus no toxicity veto makes this exactly the kind of regimen this advocate seat is supposed to surface. The honest weak spot is the small sample (n=141), open-label design, and a real cumulative CCNU myelosuppression burden — grade 3-4 hematologic AE 41% (CeTeG arm) vs 13% (TMZ-alone), driven by lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%. At 66 the cumulative cytopenia signal matters and the team should set CBC monitoring and dose-reduction thresholds up front. No treatment-related deaths in the trial. If MGMT comes back unmethylated, this pick falls off entirely and the BGB-58067 unmethylated arm or AGILE moves up.
primary_concerns: Gated on MGMT methylated. If unmethylated, this regimen has no rationale.

Cytopenia burden is the binding toxicity at age 66; CBC weekly during the first two cycles, then per protocol; consider G-CSF and platelet thresholds set in advance. No anemia or cytopenia veto in the preference file, so this is a counseling-and-monitoring concern not an exclusion.
Open-label and n=141; the HR 0.60 has a wide CI crossing 1 on the upper bound (1.03). The signal is real but the precision is not Stupp-grade.

picks.intervention_label: GBM AGILE adaptive platform (NCT03970447) — randomized backbone alternative
picks.rationale: I rank this 5 not 1 because the preference file is efficacy-leaning and trial-preferring and the AGILE platform's currently-active arms (VT1021, troriluzole, ADI-PEG 20, AZD1390 + RT, tinostamustine) do not mechanistically match this patient's MTAP or CDKN2A axes. AZD1390 (ATM inhibitor + RT) and tinostamustine (alkylator) are the most likely arm assignments by molecular subgroup. AGILE's value here is the Bayesian adaptive randomization plus randomized control against current SoC — a real benefit if the patient prefers a randomized framework over a single-arm phase 0/2, or if the Phoenix BGB-58067 slot is taken or geographically infeasible. Trial-prefer satisfied, efficacy lean acceptable, no veto. I would not pick this over BGB-58067 for a patient whose lead actionable feature is MTAP loss.
primary_concerns: No current AGILE arm is MTAP-matched. The patient could be randomized to a control arm (standard Stupp), which is a defensible outcome on this preference set but is not the highest-effect-size play available.
AGILE is multi-site and the randomization process is fast, so this is a real fallback if BGB-58067 is inaccessible.
Honest disclosure: I rank this 5 because the mechanism-matched single-arm (pick 1) carries more upside for this patient's biology than the randomized platform's current arm list.

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor, CNS-penetrant) pre-positioned for recurrence on CDKN2A-loss / RB-intact axis
picks.rationale: Pre-positioning for the recurrence conversation, not an active first-line pick. The patient's CDKN2A homozygous loss is the canonical CDK4/6i rationale and abemaciclib is the CNS-penetrant member of the class (Raub 2015, intratumoral concentrations confirmed in the Wen NCT02981940 paired-surgical cohort). The Wen 2024 recurrent GBM phase 0/2 in CDKN2A-deleted / RB-intact disease showed PFS6 ~9.7% on monotherapy — modest activity ceiling but the paired-surgical PK confirmed the drug gets to tumor at pharmacologically relevant concentrations, which is what palbociclib (Pgp substrate) did not (Taal 2018 stopped early for futility). NCT02981940 is now active-not-recruiting but abemaciclib is FDA-approved (off-label use in GBM is defensible), and the Vilgelm 2019 + AACR 2025 preclinical signal for PRMT5 + CDK4/6 combinations suggests this could layer onto BGB-58067 at relapse. RB1 functional readout is the gating step before committing.
primary_concerns: Pre-position only; patient is newly diagnosed and abemaciclib is not 1L SoC.
PFS6 ~9.7% defines the activity ceiling for monotherapy in recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM; the better case is combination at relapse rather than monotherapy.
Class AEs: diarrhea, neutropenia, fatigue. Manageable; no veto in the preference file.

picks.intervention_label: CAN-3110 oncolytic HSV-1 (Ling Nature 2023) — pre-position for recurrence if HSV-1 seropositive
picks.rationale: Recurrence-only and not enrollable at first-line, but worth ranking so the team locks the second-line conversation early. The Ling 2023 Nature phase 1 in recurrent HGG showed mOS 11.6 mo overall and mOS 14.2 mo in the HSV-1 seropositive subset (66% of the cohort) on a single intratumoral injection. The seropositive signal is roughly 2x the historical recurrent GBM benchmark. FDA Fast Track in 2024. No DLTs across the full dose range. The intratumoral-hemorrhage history is a relative caution because perilesional inflammation from viral lysis could re-bleed, and the screening team should weigh that carefully, but it is not absolute. HSV-1 serology is a cheap test to order now so the team knows the prior probability of benefit when the recurrence conversation happens.
primary_concerns: Pre-position only; recurrent disease only.

Intratumoral-hemorrhage history is a relative caution — annotate, do not exclude. Per the preference file: "Carry forward the intratumoral-hemorrhage history as a safety annotation against bevacizumab / antiangiogenic exposure." CAN-3110 is not antiangiogenic but the inflammation-driven bleed mechanism overlaps; team conversation required.
Order HSV-1 serology now to inform the future decision; no downside to that test.

picks.intervention_label: Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) on MountainTAP-5 (NCT07492680) — pin for July 2026 re-screen
picks.rationale: Not yet recruiting (planned open July 2026), but explicitly lists GBM among target tumor types, uses RANO v2 for response, and is the BMS lifecycle-managed successor to anvumetostat. The patient meets the MTAP-null gate. This is the backup if the Phoenix BGB-58067 slot is taken or if BGB-58067 hits a safety signal during the patient's RT phase. Re-screen the week the protocol opens.
primary_concerns: Not yet recruiting; can't act on this in May 2026 except to set a calendar reminder.
Brain-penetrance for BMS-986504 is not as well-characterized publicly as BGB-58067; the BGB-58067 IND has explicit CNS exposure modeling, BMS-986504 does not yet have that disclosure.
Pipeline-context pick, not first-line enrollment today.

notes: Posture: efficacy lean 0.7, prefers_trials true, no toxicity vetoes, no modality constraints, free-text says "surface all possible options for treatment" with explicit branching language for MTAP-loss and CDKN2A-loss axes. This is the dossier the advocate seat was built for. Top-of-the-list reasoning: BGB-58067 on NCT07485049 is the single highest-fit option because it is (a) mechanism-matched to the patient's lead actionable feature (MTAP loss), (b) brain-penetrant (the proximate reason TNG908 failed in GBM), (c) MGMT-stratified by design so it doubles as the methylation-decision branch, (d) currently recruiting, (e) at a high-volume neuro-oncology center (Ivy / Sanai), and (f) preference-fit fully clear (trial-first, efficacy lean, no veto). Stupp + TTFields at picks 2-3 is the SoC backbone the user explicitly asked to surface; CeTeG at pick 4 is the conditional methylated-MGMT play with the largest published OS gain in the disease. AGILE at pick 5 is the randomized-platform fallback that I am intentionally ranking below the mechanism-matched single-arm because no current AGILE arm hits MTAP. Picks 6-7-8 are recurrence pre-positions (abemaciclib for CDKN2A axis, CAN-3110 for HSV-1-seropositive subset, navlimetostat for July 2026 re-screen) so the team has the second-line menu ready. Diagnostic gates that have to resolve before locking the 1L plan: MGMT methylation (dominant effect modifier), MTAP IHC (gate for BGB-58067 and MountainTAP-5), EGFR / EGFRvIII (gates E-SYNC, CARv3-TEAM-E, Penn dual-CAR), comprehensive NGS with RNA-fusion (gates BRAF V600E and NTRK), RB1 functional IHC (gates abemaciclib), HSV-1 serology (informs CAN-3110 prior probability), MMR/MSI (gates pembrolizumab tumor-agnostic). The intratumoral-hemorrhage history is carried forward as the bevacizumab safety annotation per the preference file — bevacizumab is intentionally NOT on this rank list at any line until re-imaging and bleeding-risk reassessment, and EORTC 26101 had no OS benefit anyway. Negative-trial regulars I am leaving off the rank list deliberately: CheckMate-498 (PD-1 + RT WORSE than Stupp in unmethylated, HR 1.31), CheckMate-548 (no benefit in methylated), NRG-BN007 (futility), depatux-m INTELLANCE-1 (negative), rindopepimut ACT IV (negative), Toca 511 (program discontinued). Trials I am pinning for cross-critique conversation: SURVIVE (SurVaxM, active not recruiting), DCVax-L expanded access (manufacturability of lysate from a hemorrhage-affected resection block is unknown), TRIDENT EF-32 (closed Feb 2026, readout pending). Deliberate omissions from picks 1-8 to keep the ranked list cognitively tractable: TNG908 (terminated), TNG462 (excludes primary CNS), MRTX1719 (no GBM cohort), IDE397/IDE892 (no GBM cohort), bevacizumab regimens (hemorrhage annotation), pembrolizumab off-label (no biomarker support at diagnosis, hypermutation more likely at recurrence). Trial enrollment I would push hardest for: NCT07485049 at Ivy/Phoenix. The advocate case for prioritizing it: this is the only currently-recruiting brain-penetrant MTAP-selective PRMT5 inhibitor trial for newly diagnosed GBM with explicit MGMT stratification, and the patient's lead actionable feature is precisely the gate the trial opens on. The critique I would entertain from co-personas: single site, single sponsor, no published efficacy readout for BGB-58067 yet (anvumetostat MTAPESTRY data is the closest evidence proxy and ORR was modest at 11% in heavily pre-treated patients) — but the alternative for the MTAP axis is to wait for MountainTAP-5 in July 2026 or accept that AGILE's current arms do not hit MTAP, and at newly-diagnosed GBM the timeline does not favor waiting.

picks.intervention_label: Stupp regimen: RT 60 Gy/30 fx + concurrent TMZ 75 mg/m2/day x 6 weeks, then 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ 150-200 mg/m2 days 1-5 q28d, layered with TTFields/Optune from adjuvant cycle 1
picks.rationale: Two decades of randomized data carry this. EORTC 26981 (Stupp 2005, n=573, RoB2:Low) is the load-bearing trial with HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001) and 2-yr OS 26.5% vs 10.4%; the 5-year follow-up (Stupp 2009, RoB2:Low) confirmed durable separation at 9.8% vs 1.9% (HR 0.6, 95% CI 0.5-0.7). Layering TTFields on top gives EF-14 (Stupp 2017 JAMA, n=695) another HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001), mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%. The patient is 66 and at ECOG 1 — well within the EORTC 26981 inclusion age band of 18-70, and if functional reserve falters, the Perry/CCTG CE.6 elderly regimen (n=562, HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.56-0.80) is an evidence-grade fallback rather than a compromise. AE profile is fully characterized after 20 years of post-marketing surveillance: G>=3 hematologic AE 7% during concurrent phase and 14% during adjuvant phase (lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia dominate); pneumocystis prophylaxis is the standardized lymphopenia mitigation. TTFields adds scalp dermatitis (52% any grade, 2% G>=3) with a published management algorithm of array rotation and topical steroids. The CDKN2A/MTAP molecular signature is real and worth chasing through trials, but it doesn't change the fact that no other newly diagnosed GBM regimen has produced a comparable OS curve in a phase 3 setting. MGMT status is the one variable that legitimately re-opens this ranking — see pick 2.
primary_concerns: Adjuvant-phase TMZ G>=3 hematologic toxicity sits at 14% (n=223) — at age 66 expect dose-modification in roughly a quarter of patients; baseline and weekly CBCs during concurrent phase are non-negotiable
TTFields requires >=18 hr/day wear-time, which is a real lifestyle commitment and not a trivial counseling conversation; do not promise EF-14 OS gain without that adherence

If MGMT returns unmethylated, the adjuvant-TMZ benefit shrinks substantially (Hegi 2005: mOS 12.7 vs 11.8 mo, no statistically significant separation) — that's the conversation about a TMZ-sparing trial, not a reason to abandon RT or TTFields
Pneumocystis prophylaxis during the concurrent phase is the standard-of-care mitigation for TMZ-induced lymphopenia

picks.intervention_label: CeTeG/NOA-09: lomustine (CCNU) 100 mg/m2 day 1 + TMZ 100-200 mg/m2 days 2-6 every 6 weeks x 6 cycles, with concurrent RT 60 Gy — ONLY if MGMT returns methylated AND ECOG holds at 1 with adequate baseline marrow
picks.rationale: Conditional pick. Herrlinger 2019 (Lancet, n=141, RoB2:Some, open-label) is the strongest published front-line signal in MGMT-methylated GBM: mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.6 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, p=0.049 one-sided per-protocol). A 16.7-month median OS gain is the largest first-line GBM signal we have. The catch is cumulative myelosuppression, and at age 66 it bites: G>=3 hematologic AE 41% (n=63) in CCNU+TMZ vs 13% (n=66) in TMZ-alone, with lymphopenia at 27%, thrombocytopenia at 16%, neutropenia at 13%. The trial enrolled 18-70 and ECOG 0-1, so the patient is technically eligible, but n=141 with wide CI crossing 1.0 and the toxicity delta both argue for explicit informed-consent on the cytopenia tradeoff. I rank this above any phase 1 option only because the parent drugs (CCNU and TMZ) have decades of safety follow-up and established dose-modification algorithms; the regimen itself is the novel piece. Hard prerequisites: MGMT methylated by MSP or pyrosequencing, baseline ANC >=1500 and platelets >=100k, willingness to dose-modify CCNU by 25% per cycle if G>=3 hematotox emerges. If those don't hold, fall back to pick 1 with TMZ alone in adjuvant phase plus TTFields.
primary_concerns: Open-label and n=141 with the one-sided p of 0.049 means the OS gain is real but the precision is modest; do not over-promise the 48-month median to the patient
Cumulative CCNU myelosuppression at age 66 is the practical limiter — many patients need dose reduction by cycle 3, and platelet recovery becomes the dose-rate-limiting step by cycles 4-6
Conditional on MGMT methylated; if unmethylated, this regimen is off the table and we revert to pick 1
Eligibility tightens around marrow reserve — baseline CBC, transferrin/ferritin, and B12 should be checked before commit

picks.intervention_label: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on NCT07485049 at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix — Arm A (unmethylated MGMT + RT) or Arm B (methylated MGMT + RT + TMZ)
picks.rationale: Trial-territory pick, ranked third because it is the single best mechanistic match for this patient's MTAP-loss + CDKN2A-loss biology AND it is built on the Stupp backbone rather than replacing it. The phase 0/2 design (Sanai/Ivy) stratifies by MGMT methylation — which is exactly the branching question we have to answer anyway — and uses an SDMA pharmacodynamic readout on phase 0 re-resection tissue to confirm target engagement before phase 2. The class evidence base is shallow but informative: anvumetostat (AMG 193) in Rodon 2024 AnnOnc / Rodon 2025 Cancer Discovery (MTAPESTRY 101, n=80, informal:med RoB) demonstrated G>=3 TRAE 13.8% with treatment discontinuation 2.5% and 56% plasma SDMA reduction at C2D1 — favorable for the class, although ORR was modest at 11% across MTAP-null tumors. I have to name the missing safety datum here clearly: BGB-58067 itself has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 yet, the AnnOnc 2024 row is the closest class proxy, and CNS-exposure-related toxicity from a brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor specifically is uncharacterized. The TNG908 failure (n=23 evaluable GBM patients, 0% ORR, terminated for business reasons after CSF sampling showed inadequate brain exposure) is the cautionary precedent — toxicity wasn't the killer, brain penetration was — and BGB-58067 was engineered with explicit CNS exposure modeling, which is the design rationale that makes this trial worth the Phoenix travel and the phase 0 re-biopsy. Anvumetostat is off the table after Amgen's April 30, 2026 program-wide discontinuation; TNG908 is terminated; DCVax-L expanded access does not accept new patients post-resection because the manufacturing window from initial surgery has closed. Among the open MTAP-PRMT5 trials, BGB-58067 in Phoenix is the front-line GBM-specific option. Rank-3 reflects: layering on top of SoC rather than replacing it, biomarker-strict eligibility that already aligns with our diagnostic gates, sponsor-provided drug, and acceptable distance from the user's preferences once travel feasibility is verified. Travel to Phoenix and a willingness to undergo phase 0 re-resection are the practical gates.
primary_concerns: BGB-58067 has no published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety data yet — class evidence comes from anvumetostat, which is a different molecule from a different sponsor; CNS-specific tox profile is the missing datum
Phase 0 requires a second resection — feasibility hinges on whether the patient's residual disease anatomy and her tolerance for repeat craniotomy permit it
Single-site at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix — geographic move is a real burden for a non-Arizona patient

Requires MTAP IHC on resection tissue (mandatory after the AMG 193 four-of-six false-positive CDKN2A-only-call episode), plus MGMT status to assign Arm A vs Arm B — both gates need to clear before screening calls

picks.intervention_label: Tumor-treating fields (Optune) as a stand-alone item for explicit prioritization — already bundled inside pick 1 but called out because adherence is the load-bearing variable
picks.rationale: EF-14 (Stupp 2017 JAMA, n=695, RoB2:Some) gave TTFields the strongest mOS lift outside of Stupp itself: HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001), mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%. Safety is overwhelmingly local: scalp dermatitis under the transducer arrays at 52% any grade, 2% G>=3, with array-rotation and topical-steroid algorithms that any neuro-oncology practice runs as routine. Systemic AE rates are similar between arms, so the layering on adjuvant TMZ doesn't compound hematologic toxicity. I am surfacing this as a separate rank because, in my experience reviewing GBM cases, patients accept Stupp and then quietly fall off Optune within 3-4 months because >=18 hr/day wear-time is a real lifestyle ask. The 5-yr OS difference (13% vs 5%) shows up only in patients who actually wear the device — adherence is the dose. Ranked fourth because it's part of the SoC bundle in pick 1 rather than an alternative to it; if she declines Optune the rest of pick 1 still stands, but we lose meaningful OS gain.
primary_concerns: >=18 hr/day wear-time adherence is the actual efficacy variable, not the prescription itself — counsel the patient honestly before commit
Open-label trial design is the main bias source on EF-14; the magnitude of OS benefit is real but device-vs-no-device cannot be blinded
Scalp dermatitis at 52% (any grade) needs a baseline scalp exam and an array-rotation plan that includes the patient's hairstyle/wig preferences
Insurance authorization for Optune is non-trivial; start the prior auth at the same time as starting RT planning

picks.intervention_label: SurVaxM (survivin peptide vaccine) + GM-CSF on the SURVIVE randomized phase 2b (NCT05163080), layered on Stupp adjuvant phase
picks.rationale: Lowest-tox add-on in the dossier with a published front-line signal that doesn't compromise the SoC backbone. Ahluwalia 2023 (JCO, n=63, informal:med RoB) reported PFS6 95.2%, mPFS 11.4 mo, mOS 25.9 mo, 2-yr OS 51%, 3-yr OS 41% — encouraging vs the historical ~16-month control but explicitly single-arm phase 2a, so I cannot pretend the magnitude is fully validated yet. Safety is the standout: injection-site reactions and low-grade flu-like symptoms dominate; zero SurVaxM-attributable G>=3 SAEs (n=63). The pivotal randomized phase 2b SURVIVE (NCT05163080) is the trial that turns this into real evidence. Mechanism (survivin peptide vaccination + KLH carrier + GM-CSF adjuvant) is biologically distinct from CDK4/6 or PRMT5 axes, so it competes only with TTFields for adjuvant-phase add-on. Ranked fifth because it lacks the OS-randomized evidence of the top four picks, but it earns ranking on safety alone — the toxicity floor here is the lowest of any add-on we have access to. Note: I am NOT ranking DCVax-L. The Liau 2023 JAMA Oncology external-control analysis (HR_OS 0.80, 95% CI 0.70-0.89, ROBINS-I:Serious) reports a real signal, but the US expanded-access protocol NCT02146066 only accepts patients whose vaccine was already manufactured under the original phase 3, and this patient's tissue window from initial resection has closed. Do not raise the family's hopes there.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2a with non-contemporaneous historical control — magnitude of OS signal is not yet confirmed; SURVIVE is the validation gate
If patient also enrolls in BGB-58067 (pick 3), check protocol for vaccine co-administration restrictions — many trials exclude concurrent investigational immunotherapy
Expanded access via MimiVax exists but is more expensive than trial enrollment; pursue NCT05163080 first
DCVax-L is NOT a viable add-on for this patient because the manufacturing window from initial resection has closed — see expanded notes

notes: Position is built around three load-bearing convictions. First, Stupp + TTFields stays as the spine. Two decades of randomized data plus a well-characterized AE profile plus a 5-yr OS signal that no other newly diagnosed regimen has reproduced — that is not a backbone I will abandon for a phase 1 PRMT5 signal regardless of how mechanistically clean the MTAP rationale looks. Second, the MGMT branch is the only molecular variable that meaningfully re-opens the front-line ranking. Methylated and ECOG 1 with adequate marrow opens CeTeG/NOA-09; methylated and reduced marrow reserve stays with Stupp adjuvant TMZ; unmethylated stays with Stupp + TTFields with the explicit conversation that TMZ benefit in this subgroup is marginal (Hegi 2005: mOS 12.7 vs 11.8 mo) and that TMZ-sparing trial enrollment (the BGB-58067 Arm A is built for this exact patient) is a legitimate substitute for the TMZ component. Third, MGMT, EGFRvIII, and the rest of the NGS panel must come back before any phase-1 enrollment finalizes. The AMG 193 four-of-six false-positive CDKN2A-only-call episode at MTAPESTRY 101 is the published precedent for why central MTAP IHC is mandatory; the TNG908 GBM cohort with 0/23 ORR at active doses is the precedent for why CNS-penetration data on a specific PRMT5 inhibitor matters more than mechanism alone; the depatux-m INTELLANCE-1 readout (HR_OS 1.02, 95% CI 0.85-1.23, p=0.63, n=691, RoB2:Low) is the precedent for why strong rationale in EGFR-amp GBM does not translate to OS gain. Round 2 watch-items I will surface as vetoes or qualified dissents: (1) Bevacizumab in any front-line regimen draws an immediate veto from me. The patient presented with intratumoral hemorrhage, the Friedman 2009 BRAIN study (n=167) reports G>=3 intracranial hemorrhage at 2.4% as a baseline class rate, and the EORTC 26101 phase 3 (Wick 2017, n=437, RoB2:Low) showed HR_OS 0.95 (95% CI 0.74-1.21, p=0.65) — no OS benefit from adding bevacizumab to lomustine at recurrence. The only acceptable use of bevacizumab in this patient is symptomatic edema control at recurrence after repeat MRI confirms no active hemorrhage, after explicit re-assessment of bleeding risk by the treating team, with a documented informed-consent conversation acknowledging the 2.4% baseline intracranial hemorrhage rate is now compounded by prior bleed history. I will veto any front-line bevacizumab pick and any recurrence pick that does not surface these mitigations. (2) EGFRvIII CAR-T (E-SYNC NCT06186401, Penn dual-target NCT05802693, NCT07209241, MGH CARv3-TEAM-E NCT05660369) at front-line draws a qualified-on-toxicity from me. The phase 1 signals (O'Rourke 2017 STM n=10 with 1 long-term SD; Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 with 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity all reversible with steroids; Choi 2024 NEJM n=3 with 100% transient radiographic regression but 2/3 progressed within 1-2 months; Goff 2019 JIT n=18 with 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells) are hypothesis-generating, not OS-validated. The intratumoral hemorrhage history compounds the CRS/ICANS-mediated intracranial edema risk; none of the phase 1 readouts to date specifically address re-bleed risk in a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage. I am open to CAR-T conversations at recurrence with EGFRvIII confirmation and an explicit hemorrhage-risk-assessment plan; I am not open to front-line CAR-T in this patient. (3) CDK4/6 inhibitors in glioma deserve hard questions. INSIGhT (Wen 2023 CCR, n=73 abemaciclib arm, RoB2:Some) gave HR_PFS 0.72 (95% CI 0.49-1.06, p=0.046 one-sided) but no OS benefit; the recurrent NCT02981940 readout (Wen 2024, n=42, informal:med RoB) gave PFS6 9.7% (95% CI 2.5-22.9). That is a PFS lift without an OS lift in a population enriched for CDKN2A loss — and class AEs (diarrhea, neutropenia, fatigue) require management on top of any concurrent regimen. The Taal 2018 palbociclib failure (n=22, mPFS 1.2 mo, closed early for futility) is the cautionary precedent that CNS penetration AND biomarker selection both have to be right. I will not rank abemaciclib in my top 5 at front-line; I am open to it at recurrence on CTNI-58 or successor combinations IF CDKN2A loss confirms (it has) AND RB1 is intact by IHC (still pending in the full workup). (4) Phase 1 monotherapy substituting for Stupp draws a hard veto from me regardless of mechanism — the published precedent is CheckMate-498 (Omuro 2023, n=560, RoB2:Low), where substituting nivolumab for TMZ in MGMT-unmethylated newly diagnosed GBM produced HR_OS 1.31 (95% CI 1.09-1.58, p=0.0037), i.e. worse survival. Phase 1 trial enrollment LAYERED ON or BUILT INTO the Stupp backbone (BGB-58067 NCT07485049) is acceptable; phase 1 enrollment REPLACING Stupp is not, full stop. (5) DCVax-L: the Liau 2023 effect-size signal is real but the manufacturing window is closed for this patient (expanded access NCT02146066 requires tissue collected at initial resection under the original phase 3 protocol — see accessibility row). Do not include in any pick that implies the patient can enroll today. Final caveat on the user-preference framing: the request to 'surface all options' obligates me to keep doors open even where I would not prioritize. I have logged my reservations in the toxicity-veto / qualified-dissent stack above so the PI sees them in round 2; the picks themselves reflect the conservative ranking, not the comprehensive option menu, which will live in the consensus build.

picks.intervention_label: Stupp regimen: RT 60 Gy/30 fx + concurrent TMZ 75 mg/m2/day + 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ 150-200 mg/m2 days 1-5 q28d
picks.rationale: I rank Stupp first not because it is exciting but because, on a strict RoB2:Low + phase-3 + replicated bar, it is the only newly-diagnosed regimen that clears the bar. EORTC 26981 (n=573, RoB2:Low) gave HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001); the 5-yr update (Stupp 2009, n=573, RoB2:Low) replicated with HR 0.6 (0.5-0.7) and 5-yr OS 9.8% vs 1.9%. The catch is the Hegi 2005 biomarker analysis: in MGMT unmethylated, TMZ adds mOS 12.7 vs 11.8 mo and the gain is not statistically significant. The 0.63 HR is largely a methylated-subgroup effect being averaged across the whole trial. Important to be honest about that, but Hegi 2005 is itself a post-hoc biomarker analysis (RoB2:Some, n=206 of 573 with tissue) so I am not willing to use it as grounds to withhold the adjuvant TMZ commitment in an unmethylated patient before MGMT returns. The cleanest read: backbone is RT in all cases; concurrent TMZ is justified on the EORTC-level evidence; adjuvant TMZ is biomarker-conditional once MGMT is back. Note also: at 66, the patient sits at the upper edge of EORTC 26981 inclusion (18-70), and Perry/CCTG CE.6 (n=562, RoB2:Low, HR 0.67 95% CI 0.56-0.80) is the evidence-grade fallback if fitness shifts, not a compromise.
primary_concerns: EORTC 26981 was open-label for the chemoradiation comparator — RoB2 domain D5 (selection of reported result) is the residual concern, mitigated by OS as primary and by 5-yr replication. The trial is as low-bias as front-line GBM gets.

Hegi 2005 (n=206 of 573 with tissue, ~36% biomarker assessment rate) is a post-hoc subgroup analysis. Using it to dichotomize the TMZ decision presses against my own rule about subgroup analyses; I accept it only because the MGMT split has replicated across CE.6 (HR 0.53 methylated vs 0.75 unmethylated) and across CATNON in IDH-mutant astrocytoma.
Adjuvant-phase G>=3 hematologic toxicity 14% (n=223) at age 66 is real; PJP prophylaxis is non-negotiable during concurrent phase given TMZ-induced lymphopenia.

picks.intervention_label: Tumor-treating fields (Optune, 200 kHz, >=18 hr/day) added to adjuvant TMZ per EF-14 schedule
picks.rationale: EF-14 (n=695) reports HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001), mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%. The effect size matches Stupp itself, which makes me pause and read the bias profile carefully. RoB2 is Some, not Low — domain D4 (measurement of the outcome) is the open one because the trial is open-label (no sham device), and there is no way to blind a head-worn device against TMZ-alone. OS is an objective endpoint, which partially insulates against D4 bias, but the device-vs-no-device assignment is also known to investigators, which can influence post-progression treatment decisions in non-randomized ways. I rank it 2nd because: (a) the OS magnitude has not been replicated in a second phase 3 — EF-14 is the only positive phase 3 for the modality and I generally want at least two; (b) the >=18 hr/day adherence requirement is the dose, and the published per-protocol analyses suggest sub-18-hour wear roughly halves the benefit, so the ITT HR overstates what most adherence-imperfect patients get. Even with those discounts, the lower bound of the 95% CI (HR 0.76) still represents meaningful OS benefit on top of TMZ. Local toxicity (52% any-grade scalp dermatitis, 2% G>=3) is non-overlapping with TMZ hematotox. I will not rank it 1 over Stupp because the bias profile is weaker and the replication is missing.
primary_concerns: Open-label design (RoB2:Some, domain D4 measurement bias) — unblindable by modality. Mitigated by objective OS endpoint but not eliminated.

Single phase 3 — EF-14 is the only positive randomized trial; TRIDENT (NCT04471844, TTFields-during-RT) closed February 2026 with readout pending. I am uncomfortable that the modality rests on a single trial, even one this large.
Wear-time adherence is the binding variable — per-protocol analyses suggest <18 hr/day cuts benefit roughly in half. Counsel the patient honestly before commit.

picks.intervention_label: Perry / CCTG CE.6 hypofractionated RT (40 Gy/15 fx) + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ — conditional fallback if fitness shifts
picks.rationale: Surfaced as the evidence-grade fallback rather than a primary pick because the patient is 66 with ECOG 1 and meets full Stupp inclusion. CE.6 (Perry 2017, n=562, RoB2:Low) gives HR_OS 0.67 (95% CI 0.56-0.80, p<0.001) for the full elderly cohort. The MGMT methylation breakdown is informative and consistent with the Hegi pattern: methylated HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.38-0.73, p<0.001) with mOS 13.5 vs 7.7 mo; unmethylated HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.56-1.01) — the unmethylated CI crosses 1.0, so the benefit in this subgroup is borderline at best. This row goes in my top 3 because if treatment tolerability worsens after the first 2-3 weeks of conventional RT, CE.6 is the validated short-course alternative with the same level of evidence (RoB2:Low, phase 3) backing it. I rank it 3rd not 1st because the patient's current state does not yet require it; lock it in pre-emptively as the off-ramp.
primary_concerns: MGMT unmethylated subgroup HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.56-1.01) — CI crosses 1.0 by 0.01 on the upper bound, so the benefit of adding TMZ to short-course RT in unmethylated elderly patients is statistically borderline. Do not over-promise if MGMT returns unmethylated.
Patient is currently in the full-course Stupp eligibility window — this row is a fallback, not a primary plan.
G>=3 lymphopenia 27% is the dominant AE in CE.6, same direction as full Stupp; PJP prophylaxis carries.

picks.intervention_label: CeTeG / NOA-09 lomustine + TMZ + RT — conditional on MGMT methylated, with explicit acknowledgement of bias risk
picks.rationale: I am ranking this 4 rather than higher because the evidence quality is genuinely weaker than the top 3. Herrlinger 2019 (Lancet, n=141, RoB2:Some, open-label) reports per-protocol HR_OS 0.6 with 95% CI 0.35-1.03 and a one-sided p of 0.049. The upper CI bound is 1.03 — the confidence interval crosses 1.0 (just barely) on the per-protocol ITT analysis, and the p-value is one-sided. By RoB2 framing this is Some-to-Serious: open-label (D4), a primary endpoint analyzed per-protocol rather than ITT (D3 deviations from intended intervention), n=141 (under-powered relative to the effect size claimed), and the 16.7-month mOS gain (48.1 vs 31.4) is unreplicated by any independent trial. I do not regard the 48-month median as a number to quote to the patient; the lower bound of the gain is meaningfully smaller. That said: this is the largest published front-line OS signal in MGMT-methylated GBM, the AEs (G>=3 hematotox 41% in CeTeG vs 13% in TMZ-alone) are characterized and there are no treatment-related deaths in the published cohort, so it is not malpractice to offer it. If MGMT returns methylated and marrow reserve is adequate, this is a defensible conversation. If MGMT returns unmethylated, this regimen has no rationale at all.
primary_concerns: RoB2:Some leaning Serious — open-label, primary analysis reported per-protocol, one-sided p=0.049 with 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0 on the upper bound. The effect size is real but the precision is weak.

n=141 is small for the effect size claimed; no independent replication. The 16.7-month mOS gain has not been reproduced in any second phase 3, and the conservative read is that the true effect lies somewhere between modest and large.

G>=3 hematologic toxicity 41% vs 13% (TMZ-alone) — at 66 the cumulative CCNU myelosuppression will require dose-modification in a meaningful fraction. CBC weekly first two cycles is the standard, not optional.
Conditional on MGMT methylated. Falls off entirely if unmethylated.

picks.intervention_label: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on Sanai phase 0/2 NCT07485049 — open consideration, not endorsement
picks.rationale: I am surfacing this rather than recommending it. The synthetic-lethality rationale from Kryukov/Mavrakis/Marjon 2016 is mechanistically robust. The clinical evidence for the MTA-cooperative class is not. Anvumetostat (AMG 193) MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon 2024 AnnOnc, n=80, informal:med RoB) gave ORR 11% in a heavily-pretreated all-comer MTAP-null cohort and was discontinued program-wide by Amgen on April 30, 2026. TNG908 was terminated in November 2024 specifically because CSF sampling in n=3 confirmed inadequate CNS exposure, with 0/23 ORR in evaluable GBM. That leaves BGB-58067 as the sole brain-penetrant clinical-stage MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor with an active GBM-specific trial — and the published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety for BGB-58067 specifically does not yet exist. The trial is single-site (Phoenix), single-sponsor, single-arm phase 0/2 with SDMA pharmacodynamic readout. That is the lowest evidence tier I will entertain at all, and only because: (a) the trial layers on the Stupp backbone rather than replacing it (Arm A unmethylated = drug + RT; Arm B methylated = drug + RT + TMZ), so it does not foreclose SoC; (b) MGMT stratification is baked into the design; (c) the patient has MTAP loss confirmed and CDKN2A loss confirmed, which are the gating biomarkers. I am NOT willing to rank this above the Stupp + TTFields backbone, and I would dissent vigorously against any presentation that uses anvumetostat's 11% ORR as a positive signal for BGB-58067 — that ORR was in heavily-pretreated solid tumors, not first-line GBM, and the program is dead. Cross-tumor translation from a discontinued drug is not evidence for a different molecule. The case for trying is mechanism + brain penetration + biomarker fit + SoC-preserving design; the case against is no peer-reviewed efficacy data for this drug, single-site enrollment, and a class with two recent failures.
primary_concerns: No peer-reviewed phase 1 safety or efficacy data published for BGB-58067 specifically. The class proxy (anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101) showed ORR 11% in heavily-pretreated MTAP-null solid tumors, not GBM, and Amgen discontinued anvumetostat program-wide on April 30, 2026.

TNG908 terminated November 2024 because of inadequate CNS exposure (CSF n=3, 0/23 GBM ORR). The class's track record in CNS is two failures (TNG908, anvumetostat) and one open-label single-site phase 0/2. BGB-58067 was engineered with explicit CNS exposure modeling, which is the design rationale, but the CSF exposure data for BGB-58067 itself has not been published peer-reviewed.

Single-site, single-arm, single-sponsor phase 0/2. Eligibility requires central MTAP IHC (necessary after the AMG 193 four-of-six false-positive CDKN2A-only-call episode) and willingness to undergo phase 0 re-resection for SDMA pharmacodynamic readout. Phoenix travel is a real burden.

Mechanistic plausibility plus brain-penetrant chemistry plus biomarker match is the strongest non-RCT case I can construct for a phase 0/2 enrollment. It is still not evidence in the sense I usually demand. Open for the patient to consider; not endorsed by me as a substitute for SoC.

notes:
Calibration first. By the bar I usually apply (RoB2:Low + phase 3 + replicated + OS endpoint at conventional alpha), only Stupp clears cleanly. Stupp's HR 0.63 has been replicated in the 5-yr update and the 0.6-0.7 range holds across the elderly CE.6 trial; the effect is real and is the floor everything else must beat. TTFields (RoB2:Some, open-label, unreplicated phase 3) and CeTeG (RoB2:Some, n=141, per-protocol primary, 95% CI 0.35-1.03 crossing 1.0) are the next defensible additions, with the bias risks named honestly. CE.6 is the validated off-ramp if fitness shifts. Everything else in this dossier is either single-arm phase 1/2 or negative phase 3, and I am not putting any of it in the ranked list as a substitute for SoC.

The MTAP/PRMT5 class warrants extended commentary because the advocate seat has ranked BGB-58067 first. The synthetic-lethality biology (Kryukov/Mavrakis/Marjon 2016 PMID:26912360 / Cell / Nature companion) is robust and replicated mechanistically. The clinical translation is not. Anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon 2024 AnnOnc PMID-equivalent doi:10.1016/j.annonc.2024.06.005; Cancer Discovery 2025 PMID:39282709) gave ORR 11% in n=80 heavily-pretreated all-comer MTAP-null patients — that is an early signal, not validation, and the program was discontinued by Amgen on April 30, 2026, a fact that does not appear to have updated the advocate's framing. TNG908 (Tango Therapeutics) was terminated in November 2024 specifically because CSF sampling in n=3 patients confirmed inadequate brain exposure and 0/23 GBM ORR. Among published MTA-cooperative PRMT5 trials in CNS, the clinical track record is two failures and one open single-site single-arm phase 0/2 (BGB-58067 NCT07485049). I rank BGB-58067 at 5 rather than omitting it entirely because (a) the patient's MTAP/CDKN2A co-deletion is the precise biomarker the class is built for, (b) BGB-58067 was designed with explicit CNS exposure modeling — the proximate failure mechanism of TNG908 — and (c) the trial layers on the Stupp backbone rather than replacing it, which means enrollment does not require sacrificing the only OS-validated regimen. But I will not let the mechanism-plus-biomarker case substitute for clinical confirmation. Patient and family should hear the negative class record before counting on the upside.

The DCVax-L evidence in this dossier (Liau 2023 JAMA Oncology PMID:36394838) deserves a separate caution. The published 2023 analysis substituted external matched controls from 1,366 GBM-trial control-arm patients for the originally-randomized comparator, because the original phase 3 randomized design was abandoned after protocol modifications post-2015. ROBINS-I is graded Serious in the dossier and I agree. The HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.70-0.89) for newly diagnosed and HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.47-0.72) for recurrent are statistically separated from 1.0, but the comparator choice is retrospective and non-contemporaneous, which is exactly the bias structure ROBINS-I serious-risk flags. The Conservative seat correctly noted that the expanded-access protocol (NCT02146066) does not accept new patients whose tissue was not collected at original-resection under the parent phase 3 — manufacturability gate is closed for this patient anyway. I would dissent against any framing that quotes the HR 0.80 as if it were RCT-grade evidence.

The CDK4/6 axis in GBM warrants honest reading. INSIGhT abemaciclib arm (Wen 2023 CCR PMID:37722087, n=73) gave HR_PFS 0.72 (95% CI 0.49-1.06, one-sided p=0.046) with no OS benefit — the PFS CI crosses 1.0 on the upper bound, and PFS without OS in a Bayesian adaptive platform with non-pre-specified arm comparison is a hypothesis-generating signal, not a confirmatory readout. The recurrent NCT02981940 (Wen 2024, n=42, informal:med RoB) gave PFS6 9.7% (95% CI 2.5-22.9) — modest. The palbociclib failure (Taal 2018 PMID:30151703, n=22, mPFS 1.2 mo) confirms the principle that CDK4/6 inhibitor selection AND biomarker selection both have to be right. The molecular rationale is sound; the clinical signal is modest at best. I would not rank abemaciclib in front-line for this patient.

Negative phase 3 readouts the board must keep in mind: CheckMate-498 (Omuro 2023 PMID:35419607, n=560, RoB2:Low) — substituting nivolumab for TMZ in MGMT-unmethylated newly diagnosed GBM made survival WORSE (HR_OS 1.31, 95% CI 1.09-1.58, p=0.0037). CheckMate-548 (Lim 2022 PMID:35511454, n=716, RoB2:Low) — adding nivolumab to Stupp in methylated GBM did nothing (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.91-1.32). CheckMate-143 (Reardon 2020 PMID:32437507, n=369, RoB2:Low) — nivolumab no better than bevacizumab at recurrence (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.83-1.30). ACT IV rindopepimut (Weller 2017 PMID:28844499, n=745, RoB2:Low) — EGFRvIII peptide vaccine no benefit (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.79-1.30). INTELLANCE-1 depatux-m (Lassman 2023 PMID:35973199, n=691, RoB2:Low) — EGFR-amplified ADC no OS benefit (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.85-1.23). Toca 511 discontinued post-TOCA 5 phase 3 (n=403, negative). These six negative phase 3s are the floor: mechanism-attractive options resembling these should not re-emerge without strong reason.

Cellular therapy in this dossier reads as hypothesis-generating only. Penn EGFRvIII CAR-T (O'Rourke 2017 STM PMID:28724573) n=10, 1/10 SD at 18 months. Penn dual EGFR+IL13Ra2 (Bagley 2024 NatMed PMID:38497615) n=6, 6/6 transient radiographic regression, 0% formal RANO objective response, 100% reversible ICANS-like neurotox. MGH CARv3-TEAM-E (Choi 2024 NEJM PMID:38477966) n=3, 3/3 transient regression, 1/3 sustained at 150 days. NCI Goff (PMID:30418325) n=18, 0% ORR, 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells. None of these reach a rank above 'consider on trial at recurrence' for me. Front-line CAR-T in this patient is not supported by any of the published evidence, and the patient's intratumoral-hemorrhage history compounds the CRS/ICANS-edema concern in a way the phase 1 readouts do not specifically address.

On the negative side of my own ranking discipline: I am intentionally not including bevacizumab in any rank line. The Friedman 2009 BRAIN study (n=167, recurrent) reports G>=3 intracranial hemorrhage at 2.4%, and EORTC 26101 (Wick 2017, n=437, RoB2:Low) showed HR_OS 0.95 (95% CI 0.74-1.21, p=0.65) — no OS benefit from bev+CCNU at recurrence. Combined with the patient's intratumoral-hemorrhage history, I would qualify any pick that includes bevacizumab as a primary OS strategy. PFS gain without OS gain plus a 2.4% intracranial hemorrhage rate in a pre-bled patient is the wrong tradeoff.

For round 2 cross-critiques I will likely flag the advocate's BGB-58067-at-rank-1 with `qualified` on `evidence_quality` and `dissent` on the cross-tumor extrapolation from anvumetostat (different molecule, different sponsor, discontinued program). I will likely flag any CAR-T pick at front-line with `dissent` on `evidence_quality`. I will likely flag DCVax-L with `qualified` on ROBINS-I serious. I do not anticipate using `veto` on any picks in this dossier — none of the cited evidence is retracted or fraud-flagged. The strongest dissents will be on rank ordering (mechanism-first vs evidence-first) rather than on inclusion.

picks.intervention_label: Stupp regimen: RT 60 Gy/30 fx + concurrent TMZ 75 mg/m2/day x 6 weeks, then 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ 150-200 mg/m2 days 1-5 q28d, with TTFields/Optune layered on at adjuvant cycle 1
picks.rationale: This is the only branch every major guideline endorses at the highest evidence level for a 66F ECOG 1 with newly diagnosed IDH-WT GBM post-resection. NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 lists RT + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ as category 1 for newly diagnosed supratentorial GBM in patients age <70 with KPS >=70 (the EORTC 26981 inclusion band — patient sits inside it), and lists TTFields + maintenance TMZ as category 1 for the adjuvant phase in the same population. EANO adult diffuse glioma guideline (Weller 2021, Nat Rev Clin Oncol) and the ASTRO 2022 update concur. The OS effect anchors are EORTC 26981 (Stupp 2005 HR 0.63 for OS, mOS 14.6 vs 12.1 mo, 5-yr OS 9.8% vs 1.9% on the Stupp 2009 long-term update) and EF-14 (Stupp 2017 JAMA HR 0.63 for OS, mOS 20.9 vs 16.0, 5-yr OS 13% vs 5%). Hegi 2005 makes MGMT the dominant effect modifier (methylated mOS 21.7 vs 15.3, unmethylated 12.7 vs 11.8 with no significant separation), which the team has to resolve before locking adjuvant TMZ — but the guideline category does not change with the methylation result. This is the spine.
primary_concerns: MGMT methylation is unknown and is the single biggest variable inside the guideline-endorsed branch. Order MSP or pyrosequencing now; both EANO and NCCN treat methylation as the strongest predictor of TMZ benefit even though the regimen recommendation does not flip on it.
TTFields category 1 reflects EF-14 evidence assuming >=18 hr/day adherence; the OS curve is the adherent-patient curve, not the prescribed-but-non-wearing curve. Counsel before commit.

Patient is 66, inside the EORTC 26981 age band but at the upper end where adjuvant cytopenia risk rises; weekly CBC during concurrent and the first two adjuvant cycles is on-label monitoring. PJP prophylaxis during concurrent is the standard mitigation.

picks.intervention_label: CeTeG / NOA-09 lomustine + TMZ + RT — conditional on MGMT methylated and adequate marrow reserve
picks.rationale: Conditional. If MGMT pyrosequencing returns methylated and baseline counts hold (ANC >=1500, platelets >=100k), CeTeG/NOA-09 is the NCCN category 2A regimen for newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM with KPS >=70. Herrlinger 2019 Lancet (n=141) reports mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, p=0.049 one-sided per-protocol) — a 16.7-month median OS gain over standard Stupp. EANO 2021 names it as an option in MGMT-methylated patients with the explicit caveat about hematologic toxicity. The 2A designation is the right read of the evidence: a single phase 3 with n=141 and one-sided p at 0.049 is real but not Stupp-grade precision. The toxicity caveat is also on-label — grade 3-4 hematologic AEs in 41% of the CCNU+TMZ arm vs 13% of TMZ-alone — and at age 66 that is the binding constraint, not a reason to discard the option.
primary_concerns: Gated on MGMT methylated. If unmethylated, off the table — back to pick 1 with the TMZ-sparing trial conversation open (pick 3).
Cumulative CCNU myelosuppression at age 66 is the real-world constraint; dose-reduction at cycle 3 is common per Herrlinger 2019. Pre-set CBC thresholds and platelet-recovery rules at consent.
Patient sits at the upper end of the trial's 18-70 age band; functional reserve assessment (CGA or modified G8) is worth doing before committing to six cycles of doublet alkylator.

picks.intervention_label: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on NCT07485049 — Sanai phase 0/2 at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, MGMT-stratified
picks.rationale: Trial enrollment IS the guideline-aligned move here. NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 lists clinical trial enrollment as the preferred recommendation across every GBM treatment pathway, ahead of any specific systemic regimen at the same evidence level. EANO 2021 and the ESMO Weller 2021 update echo this — every major adult glioma guideline names enrollment in well-designed clinical trials as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM given the disease's prognosis. The trial-pick that is most defensible inside that framing is NCT07485049: a phase 0/2 built on the Stupp backbone (Arm A adds BGB-58067 to RT for unmethylated; Arm B adds it to RT + TMZ for methylated), which means trial enrollment here does NOT substitute for the category 1 SoC. It LAYERS on it. The MTAP-loss biology — patient's lead actionable feature — is the mechanistic gate, but I want to flag clearly: guidelines have NOT yet incorporated MTAP loss into any treatment-decision algorithm for GBM. The MTAP rationale is a research hypothesis. The PI should frame it that way to the patient.
primary_concerns: MTAP loss is not a guideline-endorsed treatment-decision variable in any current NCCN/ESMO/EANO version. The mechanistic case is biologically plausible but the clinical evidence base is anvumetostat ORR ~11% in heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null disease (Rodon AnnOnc 2024) and zero published efficacy on BGB-58067 itself. Inform consent has to be honest about this.
Phase 0 component requires a re-resection biopsy for SDMA / H-score readout; feasibility depends on residual disease anatomy after subtotal resection and willingness to undergo a second craniotomy.
Single US site at Ivy/Phoenix — geographic move is real. Travel is the practical limiter, not a guideline issue.

The Stupp backbone is preserved in the trial design, so this satisfies the guideline-aligned 'enroll in a trial, on top of SoC' framing rather than substituting for it. That is the read I would offer the patient.

picks.intervention_label: Perry / CCTG CE.6 hypofractionated RT 40 Gy/15 fx + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ — fallback if performance status drops
picks.rationale: NCCN CNS v2.2025 category 1 alternative for newly diagnosed GBM in age >=65, derived from CCTG CE.6 / EORTC 26062 (Perry 2017 NEJM, n=562, HR 0.67 for OS, mOS 9.3 vs 7.6 mo with the MGMT-methylated subgroup pulling HR 0.53 mOS 13.5 vs 7.7). Patient is 66 and inside the inclusion band. At ECOG 1 today the full-course Stupp at pick 1 remains the right call, but I am ranking this fourth so the team has the guideline-grade fallback locked in if performance status declines between resection and RT planning, or if logistics (transportation to daily RT for six weeks) makes the three-week course preferable. Not a substitute. A documented option.
primary_concerns: Patient is currently ECOG 1, which puts full-course Stupp in the lane. Default to pick 1 unless performance status changes or access constraints emerge.
MGMT-methylated subgroup gets the largest benefit (HR 0.53); unmethylated patients still benefit but less. Same MGMT-decision logic as pick 1.
Cytopenias under the Perry schedule run lower in absolute exposure than full-course Stupp adjuvant; at age 66 with marrow reserve concerns this is a real consideration.

picks.intervention_label: GBM AGILE adaptive platform (NCT03970447) — randomized backbone alternative if BGB-58067 is inaccessible
picks.rationale: Multi-site, Bayesian adaptive randomization, randomized control against current SoC. Enrollment in a well-designed randomized platform is the guideline-aligned move every major society endorses for newly diagnosed GBM (NCCN trial-first language, EANO 2021, ESMO). The current AGILE arms (VT1021, troriluzole, ADI-PEG 20, AZD1390 + RT, tinostamustine) do not include an MTAP-selective option, so for this patient AGILE is the second-best trial route mechanistically. But it is the second-best randomized option, period, and if the Phoenix BGB-58067 slot is taken or geographically infeasible, AGILE is where the next-most-guideline-consonant trial enrollment lives. Multi-site enrollment also addresses the single-site fragility of pick 3.
primary_concerns: No current AGILE arm is MTAP-matched. Randomization could land the patient on the standard-Stupp control arm, which is fine on a guideline-fit basis but does not advance the molecularly-targeted axis.
Multi-site infrastructure makes this a real fallback. Not a first-choice trial when the mechanism-matched single-arm at Phoenix is open.
Trial enrollment is itself the guideline-endorsed action here; the choice between pick 3 and pick 5 is about biology, not about whether to enroll.

picks.intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E-mutant disease — tumor-agnostic, conditional on biomarker confirmation
picks.rationale: Tumor-agnostic FDA approval based on the ROAR HGG cohort (Wen 2022 Lancet Oncol, n=45 HGG, ORR 33% with 95% CI 20-49, mDoR 13.6 mo, 12-mo OS 41%). NCCN CNS v2.2025 lists dabrafenib + trametinib as a recommended option for BRAF V600E-mutant GBM in the recurrent/refractory pathway. BRAF V600E is rare in adult IDH-WT GBM (1-2%), so the conditional prior is low, but the assay is on the comprehensive NGS panel already being ordered, and the durability signal (mDoR 13.6 mo) is the standout among recurrent-glioma options. Cross-society convergence is real: this is on every major adult oncology guideline's tumor-agnostic list (NCCN, ESMO, ASCO) for BRAF V600E solid tumors when satisfactory alternatives are exhausted.
primary_concerns: Conditional on BRAF V600E positivity on the NGS panel. If negative, this row falls off.
Recurrent/refractory branch in NCCN — not a front-line guideline-endorsed option even with biomarker positivity. Recurrence pre-position.
Class AEs (pyrexia, rash, fatigue) are well-characterized and manageable.

picks.intervention_label: Larotrectinib for NTRK fusion-positive disease — tumor-agnostic, conditional on RNA-fusion confirmation
picks.rationale: Tumor-agnostic FDA approval (Drilon 2018 NEJM, ORR 75% by independent review across NTRK-fusion solid tumors; CNS responses confirmed in Doz 2022). NCCN CNS v2.2025 includes larotrectinib in the recurrent/refractory branch for NTRK-fusion-positive disease. NTRK fusions are vanishingly rare in adult IDH-WT GBM (<1%), so the prior probability is low, but the RNA-fusion panel (Tempus xR or Caris WTS) catches breakpoints that DNA-only NGS misses. Order alongside the standard panel — guideline-aligned and inexpensive insurance against missing a rare actionable lesion.
primary_concerns: Conditional on NTRK fusion. Prior is very low in adult IDH-WT GBM.
RNA-fusion testing is the right assay; DNA-only NGS can miss intron-deep breakpoints in CNS tumors.
Recurrence pre-position; not a front-line option.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab for MSI-H / dMMR / TMB-H disease — tumor-agnostic, conditional and recurrence-only
picks.rationale: Tumor-agnostic FDA approvals (MSI-H/dMMR via KEYNOTE-158 and other baskets; TMB-H >=10 mut/Mb via Marabelle 2020 Lancet Oncol, ORR 29% in the TMB-H subset). NCCN CNS v2.2025 includes pembrolizumab in the recurrent/refractory branch for MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-H GBM when biomarker positive. Primary MMR-deficient GBM is uncommon; hypermutation in GBM is more often acquired post-TMZ, which makes this row more relevant at recurrence than at diagnosis. Front-line ICI in unselected GBM is explicitly NOT guideline-endorsed (CheckMate-498: nivolumab + RT in MGMT-unmethylated newly diagnosed GBM produced HR_OS 1.31, i.e. worse than Stupp). I am surfacing this only as a biomarker-conditional recurrence option.
primary_concerns: Front-line ICI in unselected GBM is contraindicated by negative phase 3 evidence (CheckMate-498). This pick is biomarker-conditional and recurrence-only.
MMR/MSI and TMB testing should be on the comprehensive panel; FoundationOne CDx is the FDA companion DX for the TMB-H label.
Recurrence pre-position; not a front-line guideline-endorsed option.

notes: Posture summary. Guidelines speak clearly on the spine: NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2025 category 1 for RT + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ in age <70 KPS >=70, category 1 for TTFields + maintenance TMZ in newly diagnosed supratentorial GBM, category 2A for CeTeG/NOA-09 in MGMT-methylated newly diagnosed GBM, category 1 for Perry hypofractionated in age >=65. EANO 2021 (Weller, Nat Rev Clin Oncol) and the ESMO 2014/2021 updates concur on the Stupp backbone for age <70 KPS >=70 and on the MGMT-stratified branching for elderly. Patient sits inside the guideline-endorsed population on age (66), ECOG (1), histology (IDH-WT GBM WHO 4), and resection status (post-craniotomy with residual disease — eligible for adjuvant chemo-RT). The intratumoral-hemorrhage history is not a contraindication for any of the picks at the rank levels I am proposing; it IS a contraindication for front-line bevacizumab, which is not in any guideline-endorsed front-line algorithm anyway. Guideline gaps the PI should flag explicitly. (1) MTAP loss is not in any GBM treatment-decision algorithm in NCCN, ESMO, or EANO. The mechanistic rationale is real and the trial enrollment is guideline-aligned because trial enrollment IS NCCN's top-of-pathway recommendation for GBM, but the MTAP-PRMT5 axis itself is research-grade. (2) CDKN2A homozygous loss is a WHO 2021 classifier (helps confirm grade 4 in IDH-mutant disease) but is not a treatment-decision variable in IDH-WT GBM at any guideline level. The CDK4/6i pre-position (abemaciclib) that the advocate seat ranked at 6 is off-guideline at front-line and barely supported at recurrence — INSIGhT showed PFS without OS, and Wen 2024 PFS6 ~9.7% defines the activity ceiling. I did not rank abemaciclib in my eight. (3) Tumor-agnostic options (dabrafenib+trametinib, larotrectinib, pembrolizumab) ARE on NCCN's GBM recurrent/refractory branch when biomarker positive — cross-society convergence is real and I have ranked them 6-7-8 as biomarker-conditional recurrence pre-positions. (4) Trial enrollment as a guideline-endorsed action: every major guideline names enrollment as the highest-tier recommendation for IDH-WT GBM. This is the framing under which BGB-58067 (pick 3) is guideline-aligned — because it sits ON TOP of the Stupp backbone, not in place of it. Where I will dissent in round 2. The advocate ranked BGB-58067 at #1, ahead of the Stupp backbone. I read that as inverting the guideline hierarchy: NCCN names trial enrollment as the top-of-pathway recommendation, but it also names category 1 for RT + TMZ and TTFields, and trial enrollment 'on top of' SoC vs 'instead of' SoC is the meaningful distinction in adult IDH-WT GBM. The Sanai trial is designed exactly this way (BGB-58067 ADDED to RT, or to RT + TMZ) so the advocate's #1 ranking does not actually substitute; the rank order alone misrepresents the relationship. Qualified dissent on guideline_fit for the rank, not the pick. Where I align with the conservative. The conservative's #1 (Stupp + TTFields) matches my #1. CeTeG conditional on MGMT methylated matches my #2. Where I might push back on the conservative's caution. They ranked CeTeG as a 'moderate' confidence pick citing the toxicity-vs-evidence tradeoff. NCCN gives CeTeG category 2A in MGMT-methylated newly diagnosed GBM — that is the collective expert calibration of the same evidence the conservative is reading, and it should weigh heavier than reading the Lancet 2019 paper in isolation. I will note this as a qualified position in round 2: 2A status reflects uniform consensus on lower-level evidence, which is exactly the right framing for a single-trial regimen with a strong OS signal. Veto territory I will defend. Front-line bevacizumab (no guideline endorses it; intratumoral-hemorrhage history compounds the bleed risk; CheckMate-498 / -548 and the EORTC 26101 OS-null result on lomustine + bev close the front-line ICI and front-line bev doors). Front-line ICI in unselected GBM (NCCN does not endorse it; CheckMate-498 HR 1.31 worse than Stupp). Substituting a phase 1 monotherapy for Stupp (no guideline endorses replacing category 1 SoC with phase 1 monotherapy at any line in GBM). I will not veto BGB-58067 because the trial design preserves the Stupp backbone. Negative-trial regulars I am not ranking and the advocate already named: depatux-m INTELLANCE-1 (negative phase 3), rindopepimut ACT IV (negative phase 3), Toca 511 (discontinued). I would also flag CheckMate-548 (no benefit in methylated) and NRG-BN007 (futility) as the front-line ICI failure record that closes that door at this line. Diagnostic gates the guideline-aligned plan requires before locking the prescription. MGMT methylation by MSP or pyrosequencing is the dominant variable. MTAP IHC if BGB-58067 enrollment is on the table. Comprehensive NGS with RNA-fusion to clear or open the tumor-agnostic options (BRAF V600E, NTRK, MSI). EGFR / EGFRvIII status if CAR-T at recurrence is being pre-positioned. None of these are off-guideline tests; all are inside the EANO 2021 / NCCN molecular workup recommendations for newly diagnosed GBM. Final caveat. The user explicitly asked to surface ALL options and has efficacy lean 0.7 with no toxicity vetoes. My role is to anchor the board to current professional consensus, not to narrow the option menu — the conservative seat carries the toxicity-veto duty and the advocate carries the comprehensive-menu duty. The picks above reflect what guidelines explicitly endorse for this patient's population; the trial-enrollment framing for BGB-58067 is itself guideline-aligned but the rank-3 placement reflects that it layers on, rather than substitutes for, the category 1 spine.

picks.intervention_label: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on Sanai/Ivy phase 0/2 NCT07485049, MGMT-stratified (Arm A unmethylated + RT; Arm B methylated + RT + TMZ)
picks.rationale: The bar is 21-month median OS on Stupp + TTFields. The upside scenario here is a mechanism-matched first-in-disease shot at the patient's lead actionable axis layered onto the Stupp spine, with a phase 0 SDMA / H-score readout that confirms target engagement before phase 2 commits, and MGMT branching baked into arm assignment. Class evidence is thin and I will name it: anvumetostat (AMG 193) MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon AnnOnc 2024, Cancer Discovery 2025, n=80) gave ORR ~11% across all-comer heavily pre-treated MTAP-null patients with G>=3 TRAE 13.8% and discontinuation 2.5% (cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record) and 56% C2D1 plasma SDMA reduction, but BGB-58067 has no peer-reviewed efficacy or CNS-tox readout yet and TNG908 already failed the GBM cohort 0/23 ORR because brain Kp,uu didn't translate from rodent to human CSF. The bet is that BGB-58067's CNS-exposure-engineered design carries the MTA-cooperative selectivity into tumor at concentrations the prior generation couldn't reach; if it does, this is the only brain-penetrant MTAP-selective PRMT5 inhibitor with a newly-diagnosed GBM protocol enrolling today and the highest-effect-size mechanism-matched play available to the patient.
primary_concerns: No published BGB-58067 phase 1 safety data; class evidence is anvumetostat-derived and the CNS-specific tox profile is unknown. TNG908 termination is the cautionary precedent — brain penetrance was the killer, not toxicity.

Phase 0 demands a second resection. Subtotal-resection block + intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation means pathology has to confirm tumor cellularity for the SDMA / H-score readout; if cellularity is poor the phase 0 slot folds.
Single US site at Ivy/Phoenix. Travel and lodging cost is on the patient — Ivy has limited assistance funds, ask the navigator (602-406-8605).
Eligibility gated on central MTAP IHC (mandatory after the AMG 193 4-of-6 local-CDKN2A-call false-positive episode) and MGMT methylation status for arm assignment.

picks.intervention_label: EGFRvIII / EGFR CAR-T pre-position: MGH CARv3-TEAM-E NCT05660369 + UCSF E-SYNC NCT06186401 + Penn dual-target NCT05802693 / NCT07209241 — conditional on EGFRvIII positivity (and Cohort 1 of E-SYNC also needs unmethylated MGMT)
picks.rationale: The Choi NEJM 2024 first-in-human readout (n=3 single-center MGH) hit 3/3 near-complete radiographic regression within days of intraventricular CARv3-TEAM-E infusion, no G>=3 AE in the lead cohort, no CRS >=grade 2, no ICANS-defining events. Two of three progressed within 1-2 months, one was sustained at 150 days. I am not pretending n=3 is OS evidence. The upside scenario is that even a transient radiographic response opens a debulking window for a combination strategy or for a second cell-therapy round, and the synNotch / dual-target / TEAM-engager generation was specifically engineered against the antigen-escape biology that killed rindopepimut (Snuderl 2011 heterogeneity, Nathanson 2014 ecDNA reversibility) and the first-generation O'Rourke construct. The play is to push EGFR amplification + EGFRvIII testing through the comprehensive NGS panel now so the second-line cellular-therapy menu is ready if EGFRvIII is positive (roughly 20-30% of EGFR-amplified GBM); if it is positive AND MGMT is unmethylated, E-SYNC Cohort 1 (newly diagnosed) is the only front-line cellular-therapy slot in the menu and is worth jumping on. Pre-resection enrollment is the highest-potential play if EGFRvIII tests positive because debulking happens before adaptive resistance hardens.
primary_concerns: CRS and ICANS-like neurotoxicity with intraventricular or intrathecal CAR-T on a patient with prior intratumoral hemorrhage is a real flag. The Bagley 2024 NatMed n=6 paper had 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity (headache, fatigue, focal deficits) fully reversible with steroids; Goff 2019 had 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells. I would not veto these on the hemorrhage history but the screening team needs explicit baseline imaging and an edema-management plan documented up front.

Gated on EGFRvIII testing (RT-PCR or RNA-fusion NGS) and EGFR amplification by FISH; both currently unknown. NCT06186401 Cohort 1 also requires unmethylated MGMT. If EGFRvIII is negative, the EGFR-amp-only Penn NCT07209241 opens at recurrence.

Single-antigen escape is the structural failure mode. Dual-target (Penn EGFR + IL13Ra2) and synNotch (E-SYNC) constructs were built to address this; the TEAM-engager (MGH CARv3-TEAM-E) recruits endogenous T cells against bystander wild-type-EGFR cells. None of these has OS-randomized validation yet.
Most slots are recurrent-only; the front-line slot is E-SYNC Cohort 1 and depends on the two unresolved gates.

picks.intervention_label: Stupp backbone + TTFields/Optune kept as the spine — RT 60 Gy/30 fx + concurrent TMZ 75 mg/m2/day + 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ 150-200 mg/m2 days 1-5 q28d, with TTFields 200 kHz from adjuvant cycle 1 at >=18 hr/day
picks.rationale: I am the risktaker, not a contrarian. The Stupp HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001) and EF-14 HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001) layered together produce the 21-month median that defines the threshold I am trying to beat with picks 1 and 2. Substituting a phase 1 monotherapy for the Stupp backbone is precisely the trade that CheckMate-498 punished (nivolumab + RT HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp in unmethylated MGMT, p=0.0037, n=560). The picks above LAYER onto this backbone — BGB-58067 Arm A and Arm B are both built on RT, MGH CARv3-TEAM-E is recurrence-only. This pick stays because the floor matters when you're swinging at the ceiling.
primary_concerns: MGMT methylation status is the dominant effect modifier and is unknown; methylated patients derive 7-8 mo additional OS from adjuvant TMZ, unmethylated patients derive minimal benefit (Hegi 2005 mOS 12.7 vs 11.8). Order the pyrosequencing now so the adjuvant TMZ commitment is informed.
TTFields >=18 hr/day wear-time is the actual efficacy variable; sub-18-hr compliance cuts the benefit roughly in half. Counsel hard before commit.
G>=3 hematologic AE 7% concurrent and 14% adjuvant phase per Stupp 2005; PJP prophylaxis during concurrent phase is standard.

picks.intervention_label: Run comprehensive NGS + RNA fusion + MMR/MSI/TMB now to unlock conditional tumor-agnostic plays (dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E; larotrectinib/entrectinib for NTRK; pembrolizumab for MMR-D / MSI-H / TMB-H)
picks.rationale: These are essentially free options. Each conditional gate has a low prior probability in adult IDHwt GBM (BRAF V600E ~1-2%, NTRK fusion <1%, primary MMR-deficient or MSI-H GBM uncommon), but the upside conditional on a positive hit is large enough to reframe the entire decision tree. Dabrafenib + trametinib in BRAF V600E HGG (ROAR, Wen 2022 Lancet Oncol, n=45) gave ORR 33% (95% CI 20-49), mDoR 13.6 mo, 12-mo OS 41% — that is a recurrent-disease readout that would totally change second-line for this patient if she comes back BRAF V600E. Larotrectinib in TRK-fusion solid tumors (Drilon 2018 NEJM, n=55) gave ORR 75-80% with CNS responses confirmed in Doz 2022 (DNA-only panels miss intron-deep CNS breakpoints — order RNA fusion). Pembrolizumab in TMB-H (KEYNOTE-158, n=102) gave ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) under the tumor-agnostic label. Even a 5% combined hit rate across these gates is worth the single comprehensive panel send-out the patient should be running anyway.
primary_concerns: Prior probability is low across all three biomarkers in adult IDHwt GBM. The expected-value framing only works if the NGS is bundled with the gates already ordered (MGMT, MTAP IHC, EGFR/vIII, RB1) — incremental cost is small but unbiased framing matters.
DNA-only panels miss NTRK intron-deep breakpoints in CNS tumors; insist on RNA-based fusion testing (Tempus xR or Caris WTS) or accept the false-negative risk.
These open second-line options at best; none changes the 1L plan unless the result is exceptional (e.g. BRAF V600E early at diagnosis).

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor, CNS-penetrant) — off-label or as PRMT5 + CDK4/6 combination at first progression, leveraging 9p21 co-deletion synthetic lethal logic
picks.rationale: The patient has the textbook 9p21 co-deletion: MTAP loss + CDKN2A loss with (pending RB1 confirmation) intact RB. That is the synthetic-lethal pair I would chase if BGB-58067 alone runs out of effect. Preclinical convergence is real: Vilgelm 2019 and the AACR 2025 TNG462 + CDK4/6 combination data show deeper regression than either agent alone in MTAP-null / CDKN2A-null models with intact RB, and the rationale is mechanistic (PRMT5 inhibition reinforces G1/S arrest that CDK4/6 inhibition already imposes). Abemaciclib is the only CDK4/6 inhibitor with confirmed CNS penetration in human GBM (Wen NCT02981940 paired-surgical PK; ribociclib also clears per Tien 2019 phase 0 PMID 31285369). Monotherapy ceiling is modest — recurrent abemaciclib PFS6 ~9.7% (95% CI 2.5-22.9) — and INSIGhT HR_PFS 0.72 with no OS benefit; the upside scenario is combination at progression, not monotherapy. Off-label off-protocol use faces a payer fight (no NCCN Compendium GBM listing) but the case is defensible with documented CDKN2A loss + intact RB + a published CDK4/6 + PRMT5 combination rationale.
primary_concerns: Monotherapy activity in recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM is modest (PFS6 ~9.7%); the combination case is preclinical and has no clinical PRMT5+CDK4/6i trial in GBM today. Off-protocol use of a brain-penetrant PRMT5i alongside abemaciclib would be a compassionate-use ask the treating center may or may not entertain.
Class AEs: diarrhea (characteristic), neutropenia, fatigue. Manageable at age 66 with appropriate dose-modification.

Palbociclib failure (Taal 2018 mPFS 1.2 mo, closed early for futility) is the cautionary precedent — wrong CDK4/6i for CNS (Pgp substrate). Use abemaciclib or ribociclib only; palbociclib is off the list.
Gated on RB1 functional IHC (still pending on the workup gate list).

picks.intervention_label: CAN-3110 oncolytic HSV-1 (rQNestin34.5v.2) pre-position for recurrence — order HSV-1 IgG serology now to inform the prior probability of benefit (Ling Nature 2023, NCT03152318 at Dana-Farber)
picks.rationale: Recurrence-only and currently active-not-recruiting, so this is a pre-position, not an enrollment today. The Ling 2023 Nature phase 1 in recurrent HGG showed mOS 11.6 mo overall and a meaningful enrichment in HSV-1 seropositive patients (~2x the historical recurrent-GBM benchmark), with durable responses in a subset and FDA Fast Track in 2024. HSV-1 serology is a $20 test, so the no-brainer move is order it now and know the prior probability of benefit when the second-line conversation comes. If she is seropositive, this becomes a high-effect-size cell-of-origin-immune-priming bet at recurrence. The intratumoral hemorrhage history is a relative caution because perilesional inflammation from viral lysis overlaps with the bleed mechanism, but the Ling 2023 cohort included patients with prior tumor bleeding without prohibitive re-bleed rates.
primary_concerns: Recurrent-disease only, currently active not recruiting; depends on trial reopening or pivoting to the successor protocol when the patient progresses.
Intratumoral injection feasibility depends on residual disease anatomy and any plan for second-look surgery. Hemorrhage history is a relative caution.
Order HSV-1 IgG now; cost is trivial and the result informs both this trial and any downstream HSV-platform option.

picks.intervention_label: FUS-mediated BBB opening (SonoCloud-9 / SONOBIRD NCT04528680) — pre-position for first recurrence at a US SONOBIRD site (Northwestern/Sonabend, Columbia, MD Anderson)
picks.rationale: Recurrent-only and requires re-resection candidacy at trial entry, so the play here is to flag US SONOBIRD sites at the patient's recurrence conversation.
